title: Least Variable Quantum Counting Processes
authors: Bita Olamaei, Florian Meier, Costantino Budroni, Pharnam Bakhshinezhad, Giuseppe Vitagliano
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26240v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Counting processes provide a fundamental description of stochastic events ranging from photon detection to clock ticks. A central question is how accurately such events can be timed when only finite memory resources are available. Here, we investigate this problem within a general framework of finite-dimensional classical and quantum counting processes. We derive a rigorous finite-memory variance bound obeyed by every classical [MATH]-state counting process, which is tight and saturated by a discrete Erlang-type ladder process. Through numerical optimization, we identify quantum counting processes that violate this classical bound, achieving smaller first-tick fluctuations than any classical process with the same memory size and mean tick time. For the qubit case, we further derive an analytical large-mean bound within a single-Kraus no-tick family, showing that the quantum advantage persists asymptotically within this class. The optimized quantum processes exhibit coherent conditioned dynamics and approach a continuous-time quantum-jump description as the mean increases. Our results establish a finite-memory quantum advantage in temporal precision and connect discrete-time counting processes with continuous-time quantum timekeeping.

title: Fluctuation--response Relations From An Emergent $\mathbb{Z}_2$ Symmetry In The Rotating Stochastic Landau Model
authors: Dhruv Kush, Nicki Mullins, Mauricio Hippert, Jorge Noronha
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26468v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we investigate the extent to which fluctuation--response relations emerge from coarse-grained stochastic dynamics alone, and which aspects instead depend on additional information about the system. To address this question, we study the rotating stochastic Landau model, an exactly solvable system describing an overdamped charged Brownian particle in a constant magnetic field, coupled dissipatively to a rotating environment, whose steady state supports circulating probability currents. Using the Martin--Siggia--Rose path integral, we show that there is an emergent [MATH] symmetry transformation that implements the time-reversed dynamics and changes the action by a boundary term. Comparison with the Crooks fluctuation theorem identifies this term with the entropy associated with transitions between steady-state configurations. After coupling the theory to external sources, the same symmetry yields Ward identities relating fluctuations and response. These identities follow entirely from the coarse-grained stochastic theory and do not fix the noise strength. Finally, upon imposing the Einstein relation, we show that they coincide with the high-temperature fluctuation--dissipation relations implied by the rotating Kubo--Martin--Schwinger condition for a microscopic Gibbs ensemble.

title: Emergent non-Markovianity In Time-delayed Waveguide Qed
authors: Stuart J. Masson Debsuvra Mukhopadhyay
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26427v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum systems are invariably coupled to a surrounding environment. A common theoretical method to simplify the problem is to trace over the environment under a Markov approximation, which assumes that the environment holds no memory over the timescales that the system evolves under. Our results demonstrate the importance of prudently making Markov approximations in quantum many-body systems, and highlight potential pitfalls to avoid in scaling up quantum devices to large system sizes.

title: Adiabatic Otto-like Quantum Thermodynamical Cycle In The Non-quasi-static Regime
authors: Salvador Castillo-Rivera Salvador J. Robles-P\'erez
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26690v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show a finite-time Otto-like quantum thermodynamic cycle that preserves the adiabatic population structure of a time-dependent harmonic oscillator in the non-quasi-static regime. abstract: ArXiv:2608.26646v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum mechanical models of resistors in quantum electronics are often based on the quantum optical master equation (QOME). title: Detuning-robust Rydberg Entangling Gates From Echoed Pulses
authors: Zhubing Jia, Yichao Yu, Xiye Hu, Lintao Li, Jacob Zheng, Christopher Monroe, Jacob P. Covey
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26446v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rydberg-based two-qubit gate fidelities in neutral atom arrays are limited chiefly by laser intensity inhomogeneity and by detuning errors from frequency miscalibration, background-field drift, intermediate state light shift and Doppler shifts. title: Fault-tolerant Quantum Computation Cannot Be Achieved With Constant Spacetime Overhead
authors: Kishor Bharti, Tobias Haug, Andrew Tanggara
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26272v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The threshold theorem states that quantum computations can be made reliable below a physical error threshold, at the cost of additional physical qubits and circuit depth. Recent work has reduced these space and time overheads to polylogarithmic or nearly logarithmic scalings, but whether the cumulative spacetime overhead can be constant has remained unclear. We further give a positive-rate CSS code construction that attains the memory bound, identify sufficient conditions under which the same scaling extends from quantum memory to fault-tolerant circuit implementations, and derive circuit-size bounds for subsystem spacetime codes. Our work establishes fundamental limits on the resources required for quantum fault tolerance.

title: Auditing Structured Randomness For Quantum Error Correction Under A Bounded Cloud Fault Model
authors: Ziqing Guo, Anthony Lawrence, Renyu Wang, Randy Kuang, Ziwen Pan
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26600v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cloud quantum processors compile submitted quantum error correction circuits and may colocate them with untrusted workloads. A fixed public encoder gives a fault-injection adversary a reusable target. Per-run reseeding changes the physical-to-logical fault map. Exact Haar-random encoders have exponential circuit cost. Efficient random ensembles provide average-moment guarantees and leave worst-case accepted corruption uncharacterized. We define accepted logical disturbance, an acceptance-weighted measure of harmful logical action in accepted results, and derive its exact Haar expectation. We evaluate a polynomial-cost seeded Clifford encoder family using dense linear algebra and gate-level stabilizer simulation against faults chosen before or after the encoder is known. Reseeding reduces mean accepted logical disturbance from 0.150 for faults chosen after learning each encoder to 0.020 for one fault chosen before it is known. The 86.7% reduction results from rejection. The fixed distance-three \([[5,1,3]]\) code corrects every tested weight-one Pauli, while 18.5% of sampled encoders in the selected ensemble satisfy exact quantum error correction. The measured reduction quantifies the integrity gain from reseeding and separates postselected detection from exact correction under explicit fault and attacker-knowledge models.

title: Exploiting Overcompleteness Of Platonic-solid POVMs For Shadow Estimation
authors: Dario Melegari, Stefano Mangini, Keijo Korhonen, Hetta Vappula, Daniel Cavalcanti
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26318v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurately estimating expectation values of observables from a finite number of measurement shots is a central challenge in quantum information science. Informationally overcomplete measurements provide a route to reduce estimation variance through optimized classical post-processing. However, the interplay between measurement geometry and dual-frame construction remains largely unexplored. In this work, we study Platonic solid POVMs ---highly symmetric, overcomplete single-qubit measurements whose effects correspond to the vertices of the five Platonic solids on the Bloch sphere--- for the estimation of molecular Hamiltonians. Using [MATH]-locally optimal dual frames, we show that the geometry of the POVM can have a non-trivial and non-monotonic effect on the estimation variance. We further propose a joint optimization of the POVM orientation and effect weights using a classical proxy state, either a product state or a Matrix Product State (MPS) approximation. We demonstrate that optimized Platonic solid POVMs can outperform standard randomized Pauli measurements, provided the MPS bond dimension is sufficient to faithfully represent the target state. These results reveal a trade-off between classical preprocessing and estimation accuracy, suggesting a practical route to improved observable estimation on near-term quantum hardware.

title: Quantum-enhanced Single And Multiparameter Metrology In Qutrit Ensembles By Generalized Twisting Dynamics
authors: Deep Datta, Sayam Chakraborty, John Drew Wilson, Vaibhav Madhok, Athreya Shankar
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26630v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum-enhanced sensing with atomic ensembles has predominantly focused on qubit-based protocols, despite the growing ability of many experimental platforms to coherently control and entangle multi-level systems. Here, we investigate quantum-enhanced sensing with qutrit ensembles by introducing three experimentally feasible qutrit generalisations of the one-axis twisting (OAT) model that involve entangling operations only between two levels, while the third level primarily acts as a spectator. We characterize the metrological utility of the dynamically generated states using the quantum Fisher information toolbox. We find numerically that all three models offer considerable freedom in encoding direction for quantum-enhanced sensing, with up to 6 out of 8 possible directions exhibit near-Heisenberg scaling after a short evolution time. We discuss experimental access to this enhanced metrological precision via effective time-reversal protocols. Furthermore, we examine the practical issues of estimation ambiguity and local dissipation, and show that they can be largely overcome by optimizing the sensor operating point. Finally, we show that the measurement incompatibility in estimating multiple parameters simultaneously encoded in different directions with near-Heisenberg scaling of precision is suppressed at the zero operating point as the system size increases. In the process, we find that one of the models enables near-Heisenberg scaling metrology with a pair of commuting generators, a possibility that arises from the [MATH] algebra and is thus absent in qubit-ensemble based sensors of collective [MATH] rotations.

result: Numerically show near-Heisenberg scaling in up to 6 of 8 encoding directions, handle estimation ambiguity and dissipation, and find suppressed measurement incompatibility at zero operating point for multiparameter estimation; one model achieves this with commuting generators.

title: Enhancing The Phase Sensitivity Of A Mach-Zehnder Interferometer Beyond The Heisenberg Limit Through Dynamic Squeezing

abstract: ArXiv:2608.26350v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a method to enhance the phase sensitivity of a Mach-Zehnder interferometer, independent of its input states. We compare the dynamic squeezing approach with existing quantum sensing protocols and show that super-Heisenberg scaling can be achieved. Finally, we demonstrate that the scheme is robust against moderate photon loss.

title: Uncertainty Limits For Post-selected Metrology

abstract: ArXiv:2608.26781v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For unitary transformations, the quantum Fisher information (QFI) of a pure state is given by the uncertainty of the generator in that state. title: Measuring The Sr$^+$ 5s$_{1/2}$ Land\'e $g$-factor Using Singlet-Triplet Oscillations In A Circular Rydberg State Of Strontium

We then show that the [MATH] chiral Majorana fermion net and the [MATH] conformal net provide Brauer non-trivial invertible quasi-local algebras, thus providing explicit constructions of non-trivial invertible states and quantum cellular automata on [MATH]. In addition, we show that the time-slice nets of rational diagonal conformal field theories admit lattice degrees of freedom, which implies the discretization of any holomorphic conformal net is invertible.
tldr: This paper develops a mathematical framework connecting invertible quasi-local algebras, invertible phases of matter, and quantum cellular automata, using K-theory to propose a spectrum of invertible phases.
motivation: To unify the classification of invertible phases and quantum cellular automata through algebraic structure, addressing Kitaev's conjectured spectrum.
method: Introduces invertible quasi-local algebras over metric spaces, defines Brauer equivalence, and shows isomorphisms between Brauer classes, invertible phases, and stable equivalence classes of QCAs using K-theory.
result: Proves the equivalence of these classifications and provides explicit nontrivial examples from chiral Majorana fermion nets and rational diagonal CFTs, demonstrating lattice degrees of freedom.
conclusion: Offers a rigorous algebraic framework that may advance the understanding of topological order and quantum cellular automata, though its highly mathematical nature may limit immediate applicability.

title: Demystifying Relativistic Quantum Collapse
authors: R. Muci\~no, E. Okon, D. Sudarsky, M. Wiedemann
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26474v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Non-relativistic objective collapse theories have been remarkably successful in addressing the conceptual problems of standard quantum mechanics. Despite substantial efforts, the project of extending them to the relativistic domain remains burdened by significant conceptual objections and technical challenges, often taken to cast doubt on the viability of the program as a whole. On the conceptual side, relativistic collapse theories have been claimed to face challenges involving tension between instantaneous collapse and relativity, frame-dependence of property values and probabilities, the possibility of superluminal signaling and the failure of narratability. On the technical side, persistent infinities, difficulties in constructing fully covariant frameworks and the apparent need for non-standard fields have hindered the development of workable models. In this paper, we offer a systematic rebuttal of the conceptual objections and provide a structured account of the remaining technical challenges. We conclude that relativistic collapse theories do provide a promising route toward a fully relativistic quantum framework that overcomes the conceptual limitations of standard quantum theory.
tldr: 该论文系统反驳了相对论量子坍缩理论面临的概念反对意见，并结构化整理了技术挑战，认为该理论是可行的量子框架路径。
motivation: 解决标准量子力学的概念问题，但相对论扩展面临概念和技术上的反对意见，可能导致该方案被低估。
method: 对概念反对意见逐一进行反驳，并系统梳理技术挑战，给出结构化理解。
result: 成功反驳了概念反对意见，并清晰地列出了技术挑战，认为相对论坍缩理论具有前景。
conclusion: 相对论量子坍缩理论是可行的，能够克服标准量子理论的局限性。

title: Lieb-Schultz-Mattis Constraints For Quantum Channels: A Spacetime-Duality View
authors: Sarang Gopalakrishnan, Yu-Jie Liu, Tsung-Cheng Lu, Frank Pollmann, Yizhi You
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26266v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum anomalies strongly constrain the possible behavior of many-body systems. A prime example is the Lieb-Schultz-Mattis (LSM) theorem, which relates UV symmetry and filling constraints to IR features of the energy spectrum and ground-state structure. Here, we ask how LSM constraints shape dynamical signatures and temporal correlations in open quantum systems. Using a spacetime duality, we show that the Liouvillian of a [MATH]-dimensional repeated quantum channel with a mixed anomaly between strong [MATH] and weak [MATH] symmetry can be mapped to a [MATH]-dimensional mixed-state symmetry-protected topological (mSPT) phase. Under this correspondence, the initial and steady states of the channel are identified with boundary states of the higher-dimensional mSPT in the presence of bulk projection. We further introduce the twisted Renyi-[MATH] correlator (TRNC) as a probe of temporal correlations in the channel and demonstrate that it is dual to the mSPT strange correlator, providing a direct bulk-boundary route to diagnose long-range temporal order implied by the LSM anomaly. Finally, we identify the , rather than the Liouvillian spectrum itself, as a more fundamental diagnostic of quantum anomalies, and show that it is dual to the operator entanglement spectrum of the mSPT.
tldr: The paper maps Lieb-Schultz-Mattis constraints in open quantum channels to higher-dimensional mixed-state symmetry-protected topological phases, introducing twisted Rényi-2 correlators as probes of temporal order.
motivation: To understand how LSM anomalies constrain dynamical signatures and temporal correlations in open quantum systems, extending the theorem's applicability beyond equilibrium.
method: Using spacetime duality, the Liouvillian of a repeated quantum channel is mapped to a mixed-state symmetry-protected topological (mSPT) phase, and twisted Rényi-2 correlators are introduced and related to mSPT strange correlators.
result: The initial and steady states are identified with boundary states, and the twisted Rényi-2 correlator diagnoses long-range temporal order; the operator entanglement spectrum is found to be a more fundamental diagnostic of quantum anomalies.
conclusion: This provides a bulk-boundary correspondence that directly probes LSM-imposed constraints on open systems, offering new insights into dynamical signatures of quantum anomalies.

title: Spectral Approximation And Ergodic-Capacity Convergence Of Hmimo Channels Under Spatial-Wavenumber Domain Mismatch
authors: Hangsong Yan, Hong Yang, Shu Sun
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26802v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish quantitative results on finite-dimensional spectral approximation and ergodic-capacity convergence for continuous Holographic Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (HMIMO) channels with square apertures and physically prescribed circular wavenumber support. The resulting spatial-wavenumber domain mismatch leads to a non-separable square-disk concentration problem for which the classical separable construction based on prolate spheroidal wave functions (PSWFs) cannot be directly applied. We project the continuous operator onto a tensor-product subspace of one-dimensional (1D) PSWFs while preserving the circular wavenumber support, yielding a generally non-diagonal but highly sparse finite-dimensional matrix. We show that the whole-spectrum approximation error, accounting for retained-eigenvalue perturbations and the residual spectral tail, remains controlled by a 1D PSWF eigenvalue-tail envelope despite the loss of separability and induced off-diagonal coupling. Beyond an explicit 1D truncation threshold, this error decays super-exponentially. This analysis further yields an asymptotic upper envelope for the eigenspectrum under the flattened two-dimensional eigenvalue ordering. We further establish a non-asymptotic upper bound on the gap between the actual ergodic capacities of the continuous and tensor-PSWF-truncated channels under their respective transmit-covariance optimizations. Combined with the spectral result, this capacity-gap bound inherits the same super-exponential dependence on the truncation order. Finally, quadrature rules with explicit radial and angular node thresholds are developed for evaluating the projected matrix. Numerical results show that conventional truncation based on spatial degrees of freedom can omit performance-relevant modes, particularly for compact apertures.
tldr: 该论文为连续HMIMO信道在空间-波数域不匹配下建立了谱近似和容量收敛的定量结果，使用一维PSWF构造稀疏矩阵。
motivation: 研究HMIMO信道的谱特性和容量，特别是在实际孔径下空间自由度截断可能遗漏性能相关模式的问题。
method: 通过将连续算子投影到一维PSWF张量积子空间，保留圆形波数支撑，得到非对角但稀疏的有限维矩阵，并分析谱近似误差和容量间隙。
result: 证明了谱近似误差和容量间隙随截断阶数超指数衰减，并给出了求积规则，数值验证了传统空间自由度截断的不足。
conclusion: 该工作为HMIMO信道分析提供了严格的数学工具，但属于经典无线通信领域，与量子信息研究兴趣无关。

title: Thresholding Post-Quantum Signatures
authors: Francesco de Sclavis, Matteo Nardelli, Marco Pedicini
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26792v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Threshold signature schemes distribute the signing process among [MATH] parties out of [MATH]. They enable a variety of applications and their research is also motivated by a recent NIST call. However, applications are dominated by pre-quantum signatures, which are more efficient but not secure in the post-quantum setting. This paper investigates existing post-quantum signatures, based on a variety of paradigms: lattice problems, one-way (hash) functions, cryptographic group actions, isogenies and multivariate systems. We propose a classification (divided by paradigm) of existing tools that are used to build [MATH]-out-of-[MATH] schemes from digital signatures. We also include general approaches based on FHE, MPC or ZKP.
tldr: This paper analyzes and classifies tools for building threshold signature schemes from post-quantum signatures across various cryptographic paradigms.
motivation: Threshold signatures are important for applications, but existing schemes rely on pre-quantum signatures that are not secure in the post-quantum setting, and NIST has called for new solutions.
method: The authors survey post-quantum signature schemes based on lattices, hash functions, group actions, isogenies, and multivariate systems, and categorize the techniques used to construct t-out-of-n threshold schemes, including FHE, MPC, and ZKP approaches.
result: A comprehensive classification of existing tools for building post-quantum threshold signatures, organized by cryptographic paradigm.
conclusion: The classification provides a structured overview that can guide the design and evaluation of future post-quantum threshold signature schemes.

title: Towards A Universal Meta-optics Solver Via Large Language Models
authors: Huanshu Zhang, Lei Kang, Yuyan Chen, Luxiang Wang, Zhaolong Cao, Douglas H. Werner
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26417v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Metasurface design increasingly requires fast models that can operate across structurally distinct device families, rather than retraining a separate surrogate for every geometry class. Conventional neural network surrogates often depend on fixed-dimensional descriptors, family-specific output formats, and repeated architecture tuning, which limits their scalability across heterogeneous meta-atoms. Here, we present a unified large language model (LLM) workflow for multi-family metasurface modeling and inverse-design. Geometries, design parameters, and optical response channels were converted into a shared instruction-following text format and used to fine-tune Gemma-2-9B across 8 metasurface families. Compared with single-family baselines, the joint model simultaneously predicted the optical responses of all metasurface families while reducing the MSE for each family by an average of 56.5%. The same representation was also used for inverse design. These results show that a shared sequence-based LLM interface can provide a practical route to cross-family metasurface design while reducing the need for task-specific surrogate architectures.
tldr: This paper presents a large language model-based workflow for multi-family metasurface design, unifying geometry and optical response prediction across eight structurally distinct metasurface families.
motivation: Conventional neural network surrogates require fixed-dimensional descriptors and family-specific tuning, limiting scalability across heterogeneous meta-atoms.
method: Geometries, design parameters, and optical response channels were converted into a shared instruction-following text format and used to fine-tune Gemma-2-9B across 8 metasurface families.
result: The joint model predicted optical responses for all families while reducing MSE by an average of 56.5% compared to single-family baselines.
conclusion: A shared sequence-based LLM interface provides a practical route to cross-family metasurface design, reducing the need for task-specific surrogate architectures.

title: Moving Forward With Multilayer Metastructures - Simple Design Of Complex Optics
authors: David A. B. Miller
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26298v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: I propose a simple and progressive way of designing and fabricating complex multilayered optics, even as we scale to large numbers of layers. The approach relies on successive layers of two-by-two blocks in which light only flows in the forward direction. It exploits a proposed trapezoidal architecture that can also support self-configuration in programmable structures, with the desired linear function or matrix set up using input vectors that correspond to the matrix rows, without any iteration other than successive single-parameter power maximizations. A key required component is a layer of 2 by 2 beamsplitters. The approach can support functions corresponding to a broad range of banded diagonal matrices. Example applications include a camera that also measures phase gradients and the direct convolution of a line of inputs with a kernel based on wavelets.
tldr: This paper proposes a simple trapezoidal architecture for designing multilayer optical systems that implement banded diagonal matrix operations.
motivation: To simplify the design and fabrication of complex multilayer optics, enabling scalable and programmable structures for various linear optical functions.
method: The approach uses successive layers of 2x2 beamsplitter blocks in a trapezoidal layout, with self-configuration based on single-parameter power maximizations.
result: The architecture supports a broad range of banded diagonal matrices and can be applied to cameras measuring phase gradients and direct convolution with wavelets.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a progressive and simple way to build complex optical systems, with potential applications in imaging and optical computing.

title: Misunderstanding Convivial Solipsism: The Necessity Of A Perspectival Logic
authors: Herve Zwirn
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26361v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Convivial Solipsism is easily misunderstood. Because it denies the absoluteness of observed events while preserving the universality of quantum mechanics, it invites objections that are often formulated in a classical, non-perspectival language. Such objections appear powerful only because they smuggle back into the discussion the very assumptions that Convivial Solipsism rejects. This article reconstructs a family of misunderstandings that arise in discussions of Convivial Solipsism, especially in connection with Wigner's friend and extended Wigner's friend scenarios. The aim is not merely defensive. The objections are useful because they identify the conceptual discipline required by any interpretation that takes non-absolute facts seriously. The central claim is that observational facts must be indexed to perspectives. A statement such as "the friend saw outcome A" is not a complete factual statement within Convivial Solipsism. It must be reformulated as "from the friend's perspective, the friend saw outcome A" or "from Wigner's perspective, the friend reported outcome B." The mistake consists in removing these indices and then treating the resulting expressions as if they belonged to a single global factual domain. This leads to apparent contradictions and to false dilemmas concerning consciousness, communication, other minds, and intersubjectivity. When that is taken into account, it appears that Convivial Solipsism is not a retreat into psychological solipsism, but a discipline of perspectival discourse. It is also shown that perspectival logic stands to classical logic as the quantum calculus of probability stands to Kolmogorovian probability theory.
tldr: This paper defends the quantum interpretation Convivial Solipsism by arguing that its apparent contradictions stem from classical assumptions, and proposes a perspectival logic where observational facts are perspective-indexed.
motivation: Convivial Solipsism is often misunderstood because objections are framed in classical, non-perspectival language. The paper aims to clarify these misunderstandings and show that the interpretation is consistent when facts are indexed to perspectives.
method: The author reconstructs common misunderstandings, particularly in Wigner's friend and extended Wigner's friend scenarios, and demonstrates that they arise from removing perspective indices. He then proposes a perspectival logic as a necessary discipline for interpretations with non-absolute facts.
result: The paper shows that apparent contradictions disappear when statements are properly perspective-indexed, and that Convivial Solipsism is not psychological solipsism but a coherent perspectival framework. It also draws an analogy between perspectival logic and quantum probability theory.
conclusion: Convivial Solipsism requires a perspectival logic to be correctly understood, and this logic is analogous to the relationship between quantum and classical probability.

title: The Role Of Geometric Analysis In Interferometer Design And Optimization For Gravitational Quantum Entanglement
authors: Alireza Maleki
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26420v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The pursuit of a quantum theory of gravity, aiming to unify general relativity and quantum mechanics, remains one of the most enduring challenges in physics. Because of the extreme energy scales associated with the Planck regime, direct experimental evidence for quantum gravity remains elusive. However, recent proposals suggest that quantum entanglement between two massive particles may provide a pathway to probe the quantum nature of gravity. In this study, we examine the interferometer geometries proposed in these works, with particular attention to the commonly used approximation that neglects phase contributions from the vertical segments of the particle trajectories. Our analysis shows that this approximation can lead to incorrect predictions and, in certain parameter regimes, to null results where entanglement would otherwise be expected. We derive exact solutions that incorporate the full particle trajectories and demonstrate that the vertical arms can significantly affect the accumulated phase. Crucially, we identify configurations in which the induced entanglement vanishes entirely, a feature missed by simplified treatments. These findings show that accounting for the full interferometer geometry is not merely a refinement, but is essential for accurately assessing gravity-induced entanglement.
tldr: This paper analyzes interferometer geometries for detecting gravity-induced entanglement, showing that neglecting vertical segments can lead to incorrect predictions.
motivation: To probe quantum gravity via entanglement between massive particles, the paper examines the accuracy of interferometer geometry approximations.
method: The authors derive exact solutions incorporating full particle trajectories and analyze the impact of vertical arms on accumulated phase.
result: They find that the commonly used approximation can yield incorrect predictions and even null results; full geometry is essential.
conclusion: Accounting for full interferometer geometry is crucial for accurately assessing gravity-induced entanglement.

title: A Stable Dg-pod Reduced-order Method For Dynamic Linear Viscoelasticity
authors: Yongseok Jang Byeong-Chun Shin
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26625v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a reduced-order modeling framework based on proper orthogonal decomposition for dynamic linear viscoelasticity governed by generalized Maxwell models. The hereditary constitutive law is reformulated using internal variables, and the resulting problem is discretized in space by a symmetric interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin method and in time by either the backward Euler or Crank--Nicolson scheme. The reduced model is obtained by projecting the fully discrete system onto low-dimensional spaces constructed from displacement snapshots. For the full-order discontinuous Galerkin formulation, we show well-posedness and derive an a priori stability bound without using Gronwall's inequality. Consequently, the bound grows at most linearly, rather than exponentially, with the final time. We further derive spatial error estimates and an error decomposition that separates the effects of spatial discretization, temporal discretization, and proper orthogonal decomposition truncation. The reduced formulation replaces the large full-order systems with low-dimensional problems, enabling efficient long-time simulations. Numerical experiments verify the predicted convergence behavior, assess different inner products for constructing the reduced basis, and demonstrate accurate recovery of transient oscillations and viscoelastic relaxation with substantial computational savings, even after accounting for snapshot generation and basis construction.
tldr: This paper presents a reduced-order modeling framework for dynamic linear viscoelasticity using proper orthogonal decomposition and discontinuous Galerkin methods, focusing on computational efficiency.
motivation: The authors aim to develop efficient long-time simulations for viscoelastic materials, which are computationally expensive in full-order models.
method: They use a symmetric interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin method for spatial discretization, backward Euler or Crank-Nicolson for time, and project onto POD subspaces from displacement snapshots.
result: They derive a stability bound that grows linearly with time, spatial error estimates, and an error decomposition; numerical experiments verify convergence and show computational savings.
conclusion: The reduced model achieves accurate recovery of transient oscillations and viscoelastic relaxation with substantial computational savings, making it suitable for long-time simulations.

title: Prompt Sensitivity Of Generative Agents: Evidence From An Epidemic Model
authors: Niyousha Hosseinichimeh Ross Williams
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26221v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As generative AI gains traction, researchers are investigating its potential to serve as proxies for humans. From undergoing cognitive psychology experiments to experiencing an epidemic, generative agents, agents powered by generative AI models, produce realistic human behavior when prompted. This study explores the sensitivity of these generative agents' behavior to prompt modifications and varied persona names of the agents. To assess this sensitivity, we use a generative agent epidemic model, wherein each agent is prompted daily on whether it wants to isolate or commingle with other agents. We found that using synonymous prompts results in negligible changes to the model's outcomes. However, minor variations in prompts, as well as contextual changes, do influence the model's results. Lastly, our data indicates that different persona names assigned to generative agents, specifically those imbued with personas, do not significantly impact epidemic outcomes.
tldr: This paper studies how sensitive generative agents based on large language models are to prompt variations and persona names in an epidemic simulation context.
motivation: The authors aim to evaluate whether generative AI agents can reliably act as human proxies in simulations, specifically in an epidemic model, given that prompt design may influence behavior.
method: They built a generative agent epidemic model where each agent is prompted daily to choose isolation or commingling, and systematically varied the prompts (synonyms, minor changes, contextual changes) and persona names to observe effects on epidemic outcomes.
result: Synonymous prompts caused negligible changes, but minor prompt variations and contextual changes did affect outcomes; persona names did not significantly impact epidemic results.
conclusion: Generative agents are somewhat sensitive to prompt modifications, but not to persona names, suggesting that prompt design should be carefully considered when using such agents as human proxies.

title: Bosonic Encodings For Hermite-Galerkin Discretizations Of High-Dimensional PDEs And Bayesian Inverse Problems
authors: Alice Barthe
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26268v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Koopman-von Neumann framework has been proposed to design quantum algorithms for non-linear dynamics. It maps a non-linear ordinary differential equation to a linear partial differential equation (PDE) governing a probability amplitude. Previous works represents this amplitude in the Hermite-function basis, equivalently as a bosonic state, and truncates the total Hermite degree to obtain a representation over [MATH] qubits, where [MATH] is the number of variables and [MATH] the truncation order. We extend this approach to a broader class of linear PDEs whose differential operators have a structured polynomial form. We prove convergence of the truncation for both time-dependent dynamics and gapped ground-state problems under explicit regularity and stability assumptions. We then introduce a qubit encoding that supports efficient block encodings of the truncated operators. Finally, we apply the framework to Bayesian inverse problems with Gaussian priors and observation noise, reducing posterior-state preparation to the preparation of a structured Hamiltonian's ground state.
tldr: 该论文提出了基于Hermite-Galerkin离散化的玻色子编码方法，用于将高维PDE和贝叶斯逆问题映射到量子电路。
motivation: 量子算法需要高效处理非线性动力学和贝叶斯逆问题，现有方法局限于特定形式。
method: 利用Koopman-von Neumann框架，将非线性ODE转化为线性PDE，并在Hermite函数基上表示，扩展至更广泛的线性PDE类，证明截断收敛性，并设计量子比特编码以支持高效块编码。
result: 证明了在显式正则性和稳定性假设下的收敛性，并将贝叶斯逆问题约化为制备结构化哈密顿量的基态。
conclusion: 提供了一种新的量子算法路线，但不在指定研究方向的直接范围内。

title: Quantizing The Guiding Center: Do Quantization And Coarse Graining Commute?
authors: Ted Jacobson Rodrigo Andrade E Silva
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26277v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a nonperturbative, group-theoretic quantization of the effective guiding center theory of a charged particle drifting in a magnetic field in two spatial dimensions, and compare the resulting quantum theory with a corresponding coarse graining of the underlying microscopic theory. In the classical effective theory, the small gyro motion is not resolved, while the motion of the center of the gyro orbit remains observable. The reduced phase space is the physical space itself, so quantization leads to noncommuting spatial coordinates, and the effective theory loses access to the metric structure of physical space, retaining only its area structure. By formulating a prescription to match between the microscopic and effective quantum theories, we find that the predictions of the quantized effective theory are generally consistent with those of the microscopic theory. However, for closed isomagnetic contours the effective theory predicts a quantization of ``radius'', a spatial discreteness absent from the microscopic theory. This illustrates that quantization of an effective theory may yield spurious nonperturbative predictions, even if that quantum theory shows no internal signs of breakdown.
tldr: This paper develops a group-theoretic quantization of the effective guiding center theory for a charged particle in a magnetic field and compares it with a coarse-grained microscopic theory, finding consistency except for spurious spatial discreteness on closed isomagnetic contours.
motivation: To investigate whether quantization and coarse graining commute in effective theories, specifically whether quantizing an effective theory can yield predictions consistent with the underlying microscopic theory.
method: The authors use a nonperturbative, group-theoretic approach to quantize the effective guiding center theory, then formulate a matching prescription to compare predictions with a corresponding coarse graining of the microscopic theory.
result: The quantized effective theory generally agrees with the microscopic theory, but for closed isomagnetic contours it predicts a quantization of 'radius' that is absent microscopically, illustrating spurious nonperturbative effects.
conclusion: Quantization of an effective theory can lead to artifacts that are not present in the microscopic theory even when the quantum theory appears internally consistent, highlighting a potential pitfall in effective field theories.

title: Critical Properties And Glass Transitions In Randomly Coupled Fields
authors: Amer Al-Hiyasat
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26279v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study an assembly of [MATH] scalar fields coupled via a quenched random interaction, equivalent to a spin glass whose spins are promoted to [MATH]-dimensional fields. When [MATH] is large, the random coupling matrix produces a family of Gaussian universality classes whose critical exponents are determined by the behavior of the eigenvalue density near the spectral edge. For a Wigner matrix, the correlation length diverges at criticality but the susceptibility remains finite, and one-loop replica analysis supports an upper critical dimension of unity. In an exactly solvable spherical variant, the heat capacity jumps at the transition in [MATH], and correlations remain pinned to their critical form throughout the glass phase, giving generic scale invariance despite the absence of a Goldstone mode.
tldr: This paper analyzes critical properties and glass transitions in a system of scalar fields with quenched random couplings, revealing Gaussian universality classes and scale invariance in the glass phase.
motivation: To understand critical behavior and glass transitions in disordered systems with random couplings, extending spin glass models to field-theoretic settings.
method: The study employs random matrix theory for the coupling matrix, replica analysis, and an exact spherical variant to derive critical exponents and thermodynamic quantities.
result: For Wigner matrices, the correlation length diverges at criticality but susceptibility remains finite; an upper critical dimension of unity is suggested. In the spherical model, the heat capacity jumps and correlations stay critical across the glass phase, implying generic scale invariance.
conclusion: The system exhibits a family of Gaussian universality classes and scale invariance without a Goldstone mode, providing insights into glass transitions in random-field systems.

title: Information-theoretic Formulation Of The Traveling Salesman Problem
authors: Enrico Maria Fenoaltea, Riccardo Piombo, Aurelio Patelli
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26339v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) asks for the shortest route to visit a set of cities exactly once. It combines a simple local rule - each city must be visited once - with a hard, global constraint- all cities must be traversed within a single cycle. We cast the problem within a probabilistic, information-theoretic framework. The coexistence of local and global constraints is precisely what makes the problem difficult to address in this framework: the local rule can be enforced through vertex-level constraints, whereas the global constraint cannot be captured by independent edge probabilities. We show that this obstacle can be overcome by defining a maximum-entropy probability distribution over graphs, in which edge costs and degree constraints generate an assignment-like ensemble, and a global term, describing the hard constraint, tilts this ensemble toward Hamiltonian cycles. To make the construction tractable, we derive a mean-field approximation in terms of edge occupancies and implement a differentiable cycle penalty that suppresses sub-tours. This leads to a self-consistent numerical procedure whose output is not only a candidate tour but also a probability matrix encoding competing edges and degenerate solutions. We test the method on synthetic ensembles and on TSPLIB instances. The algorithm converges to connected tours in polynomial time, matching the best-known solution in the majority of instances and remaining within a small relative gap otherwise. Beyond its competitive performance, the proposed framework offers a general approach for handling hard constraints while reducing hard combinatorial optimization problems to simpler ones.
tldr: This paper presents an information-theoretic approach to the Traveling Salesman Problem using maximum entropy distributions and mean-field approximation to find Hamiltonian cycles.
motivation: The authors aim to combine local and global constraints in TSP within a probabilistic framework, addressing the challenge that global cycle constraints cannot be captured by independent edge probabilities.
method: They define a maximum-entropy probability distribution over graphs with edge costs and degree constraints, add a differentiable cycle penalty, and derive a mean-field approximation in terms of edge occupancies.
result: The algorithm converges to connected tours in polynomial time, matching best-known solutions on the majority of tested TSPLIB instances and remaining within a small relative gap otherwise.
conclusion: The framework offers a general approach for handling hard constraints in combinatorial optimization, reducing them to simpler problems while providing a probability matrix that encodes competing solutions.

title: Loss-tolerant Hybrid Metasurface Mirror For Reducing Coating Brownian Noise In Precision Optical Cavities
authors: Swadha Pandey, Evan D. Hall, Peter Fritschel, Matthew Evans
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26370v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a hybrid mirror design that places an embedded metasurface beneath a Bragg reflector, combining the low coating Brownian noise of metasurface mirrors with the low optical loss of conventional multilayer coatings. Unlike previous hybrid designs, which place the metasurface at the input surface, our design positions it below the Bragg stack, reducing the optical field incident on the loss-prone resonant layer. For a design operating at 1064 nm, we show that this reduces absorption from 24 ppm for a bare metasurface to 7 ppm for the hybrid. We introduce a general method for calculating the coating Brownian noise of hybrid metasurface-multilayer mirrors at arbitrary coupling strength, extending prior methods to coherently combine a beam-scale mean-field contribution with the periodic, sub-wavelength-scale response of the metasurface. Applying this to our design, we find a reduction in Brownian noise amplitude spectral density relative to an equivalent-reflectance Bragg mirror by a factor of 1.6. Finally, we show that this design has higher angular tolerance than a bare metasurface mirror, maintaining higher reflectance over an angular range of 1 degree. This work provides a practical path towards incorporating low-noise metasurface mirrors into precision optical cavities, while minimizing optical loss and angular sensitivity.
tldr: This paper proposes a hybrid mirror design with an embedded metasurface beneath a Bragg reflector to reduce coating Brownian noise in precision optical cavities while minimizing optical loss.
motivation: Precision optical cavities suffer from coating Brownian noise, which can be reduced by metasurface mirrors, but such mirrors have high optical loss. A hybrid design aims to combine low noise with low loss.
method: The authors place a metasurface below the Bragg stack and develop a general method to compute coating Brownian noise for hybrid metasurface-multilayer mirrors, coherently combining mean-field and periodic subwavelength responses.
result: The design reduces absorption from 24 ppm to 7 ppm at 1064 nm, lowers Brownian noise amplitude spectral density by a factor of 1.6 relative to an equivalent Bragg mirror, and maintains high reflectance over a 1-degree angular range.
conclusion: The hybrid metasurface mirror offers a practical path to integrating low-noise metasurface mirrors into precision optical cavities without excessive loss or angular sensitivity.

title: Large Deviations For The Bose--Einstein Condensate Of The Ideal Gas In The Canonical Ensemble
authors: Xuanyu Li Andreas Deuchert
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26378v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a non-interacting Bose gas governed by a general one-particle Hamiltonian in the canonical ensemble. Our main results are large-deviation estimates for the number of particles in the Bose--Einstein condensate. We show that the left- and right-tail probabilities decay at different exponential rates as the number of particles tends to infinity.
tldr: This paper derives large deviation estimates for the number of particles in the Bose-Einstein condensate of a non-interacting Bose gas in the canonical ensemble.
motivation: The goal is to understand the probability of large fluctuations in the condensate number, which is important for a rigorous characterization of Bose-Einstein condensation.
method: The authors employ large deviation theory for the canonical ensemble, considering a general one-particle Hamiltonian for the ideal Bose gas.
result: They show that the left- and right-tail probabilities decay exponentially with different rates as the number of particles tends to infinity.
conclusion: The work provides a complete characterization of large deviations for the condensate number, extending existing results and clarifying the asymptotic behavior of fluctuations.

title: Optically Induced Thermal Runaway In Phase-Change Vo2 Nanostructures
authors: Ji\v{r}\'i Kab\'at, Peter Kepi\v{c}, Andrea Kone\v{c}n\'a, Filip Ligmajer
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26401v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While thermal runaway occurs across diverse physical disciplines, its presence in subwavelength phase-change photonics remains unexplored because existing thermo-optical models break down near sharp optical transitions. Here, we introduce an iterative multiphysics framework coupling full-wave electrodynamics with heat transfer, and we discover optically induced thermal runaway in vanadium dioxide (VO2) nanostructures. The runaway switching threshold depends on the illumination wavelength, ambient temperature, and underlying substrate, with external thermal biasing significantly reducing the optical intensity required for runaway ignition. Our results push forward the modeling of sharp photothermal transitions and provide essential design principles for active metasurfaces, neuromorphic photonic devices, and nanoscale thermal management.
tldr: Introduces an iterative multiphysics framework to model and discover optically induced thermal runaway in VO2 nanostructures, with implications for active metasurfaces and neuromorphic photonics.
motivation: Existing thermo-optical models fail near sharp optical transitions, leaving thermal runaway in subwavelength phase-change photonics unexplored.
method: Couples full-wave electrodynamics with heat transfer in an iterative framework to simulate photothermal responses.
result: Shows switching threshold depends on wavelength, ambient temperature, and substrate, and can be reduced by external thermal biasing.
conclusion: Provides essential design principles for active metasurfaces, neuromorphic photonic devices, and nanoscale thermal management.

title: A Closure Criterion For Electromagnetic Curves On The Sphere In A Uniform Ambient Field
authors: C S L\'opez-Monsalvo
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26412v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the motion of a charged test particle confined to the round unit sphere in a uniform ambient magnetic field. We use an extension of Noether's theorem for systems with magnetic forces to reduce the problem to a quadrature. The rotation number of a trajectory, the azimuth it gains over one oscillation in latitude, is a complete elliptic integral of the third kind in Legendre form. A trajectory closes if and only if that advance is a rational multiple of a full turn. The criterion holds on every level set of the two first integrals. Then, we differentiate the rotation number with respect to the half-cyclotron frequency and sign that derivative on each of the two branches into which a level set divides. The rotation number sees the charge, the mass, the field and the speed through a single dimensionless ratio, that of the half-cyclotron frequency to the speed. A closed trajectory therefore fixes a value of that ratio. We say how many values carry a given rational winding. The poles are attainable on a single level set, where the motion reduces to a pendulum. The field has no flux through the sphere, so it is globally exact. We compute the Ma\~n\'e strict critical value of the resulting exact magnetic flow. Above that value the closed trajectories are closed Reeb orbits of an explicit contact form.
tldr: This paper studies the motion of a charged particle on a sphere in a uniform magnetic field and derives a closure criterion based on the rotation number.
motivation: The authors aim to understand periodic orbits of charged particles in magnetic fields on curved spaces, extending classical mechanics results.
method: They use an extension of Noether's theorem to reduce the problem to quadrature and express the rotation number as a complete elliptic integral of the third kind.
result: A trajectory closes if and only if the rotation number is a rational multiple of a full turn; the number of rational windings for a given value is determined.
conclusion: The paper provides a complete closure criterion and connects the magnetic flow to Reeb orbits and the Mañé critical value.

title: Phase Retrieval Based On Intensity-only Spatiotemporal Wavefront Shaping
authors: Luis Alberto Razo-L\'opez, Marc Guillon, Fabrice Lemoult, S\'ebastien M. Popoff
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26445v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a phase retrieval method based on harmonic field representations generated by intensity-only spatiotemporal modulation. A periodic amplitude angular modulation encodes phase information into temporal intensity harmonics, enabling wavefront reconstruction without interferometry, reference beams, or a calibrated phase modulator. We consider a disordered system that can be modeled as a phase plate and measure the intensity pattern in the far field for a rotating excitation pattern generated by a digital micromirror device (DMD). We extract the harmonic components of the spatiotemporal speckle and exploit a gradient-based optimization algorithm to retrieve both the optical phase in the plane of the camera corresponding to a plane-wave illumination and the effective phase plate that represents the disordered system. We demonstrate experimentally the accuracy of the approach in quantitatively estimating and compensating for phase distortion ranging from low-spatial-frequency aberrations to high-frequency distortions of a ground-glass diffuser. The proposed approach establishes a new route toward calibration-free phase retrieval using intensity-only measurements.
tldr: This paper introduces a calibration-free phase retrieval method using intensity-only spatiotemporal modulation and harmonic decomposition, demonstrated experimentally on disordered media.
motivation: To develop a phase retrieval technique that avoids interferometry, reference beams, and calibrated phase modulators, enabling simpler and more robust wavefront reconstruction.
method: A periodic amplitude angular modulation with a DMD encodes phase into temporal intensity harmonics; harmonic components of the spatiotemporal speckle are extracted and a gradient-based optimization reconstructs the phase and effective phase plate.
result: Experimental demonstration accurately estimates and compensates phase distortions from low-spatial-frequency aberrations to high-frequency ground-glass diffuser distortions.
conclusion: The approach provides a new route for calibration-free phase retrieval using only intensity measurements, useful for wavefront shaping in complex media.

title: HoloCMA: A Holographic Eye On Coarse-Mode Aerosols
authors: Nikil Krishnakumar, Ryne A. Juidici, Nicholas Bravo-Frank, Shibo Wang, Qisheng Ou, Francisco J. Romayb, Wing Lai, Chongai Kuang, Naruki Hiranuma, David Y. H. Pui, Jiarong Hong
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26466v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coarse-mode aerosols (CMAs), including pollen, spores, and dust, remain difficult to characterize in situ because conventional instruments rarely resolve particle geometry and number concentration together. We present HoloCMA, which combines digital inline holography, numerical reconstruction, and deep learning-assisted analysis for particle-resolved measurement. Its optical system targets particles from approximately 5.0 um to the millimeter scale. HoloCMA supports active sampling at up to 30.0 L/min and converts to open-path operation by removing the sampling module. With an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Laptop GPU and 8 GB VRAM, HoloCMA reports equivalent circular diameter (ECD) and number concentration in real time without sustained queue buildup up to 11.4 particles/cm3. Additional computing could extend real-time analysis to the workflow limit of 100.0 particles/cm3. We evaluated HoloCMA using polystyrene latex spheres, sodium chloride and ammonium sulfate crystals, and oleic acid droplets with nominal diameters of 4.9-11.8 um, with an Aerodynamic Particle Sizer (APS) for comparison. Across 12 comparisons, absolute differences between HoloCMA and corrected APS geometric-mean diameters ranged from less than 0.1 to 1.0 um, with a mean absolute difference of 0.5 um and a mean absolute relative difference of 8.4%. HoloCMA measures geometric size directly from reconstructed contours, whereas converting APS aerodynamic diameter requires material-specific assumptions. The APS-to-HoloCMA concentration ratio generally decreased with particle size, consistent with size-dependent transport and counting losses in the APS, although the cause could not be determined conclusively. HoloCMA thus enables continuous CMA measurements that combine geometric size, number concentration, and retained particle images, supporting classification and long-term atmospheric, environmental, and indoor-air monitoring.
tldr: This paper presents HoloCMA, a digital inline holography system with deep learning for real-time measurement of coarse-mode aerosols, achieving geometric size and concentration measurements.
motivation: Coarse-mode aerosols are difficult to characterize in situ due to limitations in resolving particle geometry and concentration simultaneously.
method: HoloCMA combines digital inline holography, numerical reconstruction, and deep learning analysis to measure particle size and concentration, validated against an Aerodynamic Particle Sizer.
result: The system measured geometric diameters with mean absolute relative difference of 8.4% compared to corrected APS, and supports real-time analysis up to 11.4 particles/cm3 with a laptop GPU.
conclusion: HoloCMA enables continuous, particle-resolved measurements of coarse-mode aerosols, with potential for atmospheric and environmental monitoring.

title: Dynamical Classical-field Limit Of Bosonic Gibbs States: Renormalized Hartree Nls Correlations In 2d And 3d
authors: Phan Th\`anh Nam, Rongchan Zhu, Xiangchan Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26477v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we derive the time-dependent correlation functions of the renormalized Hartree NLS equation on the torus [MATH], [MATH], from the corresponding bosonic many-body Gibbs dynamics. In contrast with the 1D problem studied earlier by Fr\"ohlich, Knowles, Schlein and Sohinger, in higher dimensions the scaled quantum particle number is not uniformly bounded and the relevant classical fields require Wick renormalization. Our proof combines convergence of the quantum generators in weighted Hilbert spaces with uniqueness for positive solutions of the limiting Liouville equation that are dominated by the Gibbs measure.
tldr: This paper derives time-dependent correlation functions of the renormalized Hartree NLS equation from bosonic many-body Gibbs dynamics in 2D and 3D, requiring Wick renormalization.
motivation: To extend the classical field limit of bosonic Gibbs states to higher dimensions, where the particle number is not uniformly bounded and Wick renormalization is necessary.
method: Combines convergence of quantum generators in weighted Hilbert spaces with uniqueness for positive solutions of the limiting Liouville equation dominated by the Gibbs measure.
result: Successfully derives the renormalized Hartree NLS correlations from the many-body Gibbs dynamics in 2D and 3D.
conclusion: Extends previous 1D results to higher dimensions, addressing the need for renormalization in bosonic many-body systems.

title: Beyond Geometric Symmetry: Broadband Linear Relations In Wave Scattering
authors: Malte R\"ontgen, Sucui Luo, Xuelong Chen, Chenyu Zhang, Ruotao Ye, Tianshu Jiang, Wenlong Gao
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26562v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The design and control of wave scattering, that is, of the reflection and transmission parameters of a device, is of ubiquitous importance. These parameters generally change with varying frequency, though certain linear relations may exist between them. Reciprocity and geometric symmetry (reflections, rotations, etc.) are classic and well-known examples that are present in many devices and significantly ease their design. In this work, we go beyond these and introduce a new class of relations that cannot be induced by reciprocity or geometric symmetry. Choosing networks of waveguides as our workhorse, we discuss the conditions and consequences of such novel behaviour and showcase suitable example setups. We further experimentally test our predictions using coaxial cables and find excellent agreement in the broad frequency range between 0 and 1 GHz. Our work not only deepens the theoretical understanding of waveguide network dynamics, but also opens new avenues for applications in broadband signal processing, quantum information, and integrated photonics.
tldr: This paper introduces a new class of linear relations in wave scattering beyond reciprocity and geometric symmetry, demonstrated in waveguide networks and verified experimentally with coaxial cables.
motivation: To find new design principles for wave scattering devices beyond known symmetry-induced relations, enabling more flexible control of reflection and transmission parameters.
method: The authors theoretically analyze waveguide networks to derive conditions for the new relations, then experimentally test them using coaxial cables over a broad frequency range (0-1 GHz).
result: Excellent agreement between theory and experiment confirms the existence of these novel relations in a broad frequency range.
conclusion: The work deepens understanding of waveguide network dynamics and opens new avenues for applications in broadband signal processing, quantum information, and integrated photonics.

title: Directional Emission From High-Q Asymmetric Hollow Whispering Gallery Resonators
authors: Amal Jose, Ramgopal Madugani, Christophe Pin, S\'ile Nic Chormaic
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26691v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Whispering gallery mode (WGM) resonators with broken rotational symmetry exhibit phenomena that are generally absent in conventional symmetric cavities, including directional emission. While such effects have been extensively investigated in solid and planar resonators, they remain largely unexplored in hollow, three-dimensional cavities, where optical confinement is fundamentally altered by the thin wall geometry. Here, we demonstrate controlled fabrication of asymmetric silica microbubble resonators through anisotropic expansion during the microbubble formation process. X-ray tomography confirms the resulting three-dimensional geometry and allows us to quantitatively characterize the cavity deformation. Despite the broken rotational symmetry, the resonators maintain whispering gallery modes with high loaded Q-factors exceeding [MATH] for moderate deformations. Optical characterization reveals that only certain resonances exhibit directional emission, whereas neighboring modes retain conventional isotropic behavior. Two-dimensional numerical simulations reproduce the observed emission characteristics and indicate that deformation-induced leakage of higher-order modes provides a plausible mechanism for the directional radiation. These results establish asymmetric hollow microbubble resonators as a platform for investigating light transport in three-dimensional asymmetric whispering gallery cavities while preserving the high-Q performance required for photonics applications.
tldr: This paper demonstrates the fabrication of asymmetric hollow microbubble resonators that maintain high Q-factors and exhibit directional emission from certain modes due to deformation-induced leakage.
motivation: Directional emission from whispering gallery mode resonators with broken symmetry has been studied in solid and planar cavities but not in hollow three-dimensional cavities where confinement is altered by thin walls.
method: Asymmetric silica microbubbles were fabricated via anisotropic expansion, characterized by X-ray tomography, and optical measurements were performed; 2D simulations replicated the observed emission.
result: High loaded Q-factors were maintained for moderate deformations, and only specific resonances emitted directionally while others were isotropic.
conclusion: Asymmetric hollow microbubble resonators provide a platform for investigating light transport in 3D asymmetric whispering gallery cavities while preserving high-Q performance.

title: Brownian Yet non-Gaussian Diffusion Through Equilibrium Nonlinear Friction
authors: Andreas M. Menzel Jakob Mihatsch
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26773v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In Brownian yet non-Gaussian diffusion (BnGD) the mean squared displacement grows linearly in time. However, the displacement statistics do not follow a normal distribution throughout. Typically, they are non-Gaussian at intermediate times, before they cross over to Gaussian in the long-time regime. We demonstrate that nonlinear friction under correctly applied stochastic equilibrium conditions provides an explanation of this phenomenon also for homogeneous environments.
tldr: 该论文通过非线性摩擦和平衡态条件解释了均匀环境中布朗但非高斯扩散现象。
motivation: 布朗但非高斯扩散（BnGD）现象在中间时间表现出非高斯统计，但传统解释通常需要非均匀环境，该论文旨在展示该现象也可在均匀环境中由非线性摩擦引起。
method: 作者在随机运动模型中引入非线性摩擦，并正确应用平衡态条件进行分析，推导了位移统计量随时间演化。
result: 模型表明非线性摩擦可导致非高斯扩散，且最终在长时间极限下过渡到高斯行为。
conclusion: 研究提供了一种新的机制解释BnGD，并强调了平衡态条件下非线性摩擦的重要性。

title: Dual-Symmetrized Construction Of Electromagnetic Beams Beyond The Paraxial Approximation With An Explicit Separation Of Scalar And Vectorial Corrections
authors: Kayn A. Forbes Abdullah F. Alharbi
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26776v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a perturbative framework for constructing the fields of electromagnetic beams beyond the paraxial approximation, in which the vectorial correction is shared symmetrically between the electric and magnetic fields and separated from the isotropic scalar correction. The method is based on a direct iterative derivation from Maxwell equations and combines complementary electric-first and magnetic-first constructions, thereby removing the construction-dependent assignment of the vectorial correction to either the electric or magnetic field. In addition, the scalar envelope correction is obtained independently from the isotropic co-polar contribution to the solutions of the higher-order Helmholtz equation. The resulting corrected fields apply to an arbitrary paraxial envelope and input Jones polarization.
tldr: A perturbative framework for beyond-paraxial electromagnetic beams with symmetrized vectorial corrections and separate scalar corrections.
motivation: To improve beyond-paraxial descriptions of electromagnetic beams and remove construction-dependent assignment of vectorial corrections.
method: Iterative derivation from Maxwell equations combining electric-first and magnetic-first constructions, with scalar correction from the Helmholtz equation.
result: A general framework applicable to arbitrary paraxial envelopes and Jones polarizations.
conclusion: Provides a more symmetric and general construction for beyond-paraxial beam fields.

title: Observing Relativistic Trajectories Of Single Photons
authors: Sayantan Das, Daniel S. Dahl, Daniel Peace, Marcelo P. Almeida, Abhishek Roy, Markus Rambach, Andrew G. White, Timothy C. Ralph, Jacquiline Romero
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26778v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While the standard interpretation of quantum mechanics does not assign definite trajectories to particles, the Bohmian interpretation does. Only recently has an operational method for reconciling Bohmian mechanics with relativity been proposed. Here, we experimentally reconstruct relativistic Bohmian trajectories of a single photon in a Michelson-Sagnac interferometer, where counter-propagating probability amplitudes interfere head-on at the speed of light. As predicted by the relativistic Bohmian theory, we observe subluminal and superluminal features of the Bohmian trajectories of the photon traversing through the fringes. Our work provides experimental access to relativistic Bohmian mechanics and enables exploration of its unusual and counterintuitive properties.
tldr: Experimental reconstruction of relativistic Bohmian trajectories for single photons in an interferometer.
motivation: To provide experimental access to relativistic Bohmian mechanics and test its predictions, which are counterintuitive yet reconcilable with relativity.
method: Using a Michelson-Sagnac interferometer with counter-propagating probability amplitudes, the researchers reconstructed photon trajectories based on relativistic Bohmian theory.
result: Observed subluminal and superluminal features of the Bohmian trajectories as predicted by the theory.
conclusion: The experiment demonstrates the feasibility of observing relativistic Bohmian trajectories, offering new insights into quantum interpretations and their relativistic extensions.

title: A Simple Algorithm For The Summation Of Alternating Series
authors: Eleonora Denich, Paolo Novati, Alvise Sommariva
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26287v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper deals with the computation of the sum of alternating series, whose general terms can be expressed by means of analytic functions. After rewriting the series as a weighted integral with the Abel weight, we employ the sinc (trapezoidal) rule and analyze the remainder term with respect to the number of quadrature points. We provide some numerical experiments to show the reliability of the derived error estimate and to test the algorithm for automatic summation with prescribed accuracy. All the Matlab codes used in the present paper can be found as open-source software at the authors' homepage.
tldr: The paper presents a simple algorithm for summing alternating series using the sinc rule with reliable error estimates.
motivation: To provide a simple and reliable method for automatic summation of alternating series with prescribed accuracy.
method: The series is rewritten as a weighted integral with the Abel weight, and the sinc (trapezoidal) rule is applied; the remainder term is analyzed as a function of quadrature points.
result: Numerical experiments demonstrate the reliability of the derived error estimate and the algorithm's effectiveness for automatic summation.
conclusion: The algorithm is open-sourced in Matlab, offering a practical tool for computing sums of alternating series.

title: Decoding Algorithms For Mds Array Codes
authors: Sara D. Cardell, Gustavo Terra Bastos, Cintya Wink de Oliveira Benedito
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26483v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study decoding procedures for a family of MDS array codes previously constructed from the Kronecker product of a superregular matrix and a non-singular matrix over a finite field. By exploiting the particular structure of their parity-check matrices, we develop decoding algorithms for different channel models. For the erasure channel, we provide an algorithm capable of recovering any pattern of up to [MATH] symbol erasures. For the [MATH]-ary symmetric channel, we investigate the decoding of one and two symbol errors and give explicit procedures for determining their locations and values. We also consider the particular case in which the superregular matrix is a Vandermonde matrix, showing how its additional algebraic structure can be exploited in the decoding process. Explicit examples over different finite fields are provided to illustrate the proposed procedures.
tldr: This paper presents decoding algorithms for MDS array codes over finite fields, focusing on erasure and symmetric channel error correction.
motivation: To develop efficient decoding procedures for a family of MDS array codes constructed via Kronecker products.
method: Exploits the structure of parity-check matrices to design decoding algorithms for erasure and symmetric channels, including specific cases with Vandermonde matrices.
result: An algorithm for recovering any pattern of up to a certain number of symbol erasures, and procedures for one and two symbol errors on the symmetric channel.
conclusion: The paper provides explicit decoding procedures with illustrative examples.

title: Physics-Informed Stochastic Configuration Machine: A Backpropagation-Free Neural Network With Fast Training For Nonlinear Differential Equations
authors: Yuehao Song (school Of Automation, Central South University, Changsha, China), Zhong Chen (school Of Automation, Central South University, Changsha, China), Lihui Cen (school Of Automation, Central South University, Changsha, China), Liang Wu (johns Hopkins University, Baltimore, USA), Kai Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26549v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have emerged as a transformative paradigm for solving complex differential equations, their reliance on backpropagation-based gradient descent and automatic differentiation (AD) imposes significant computational bottlenecks and severe non-convex optimization challenges. To overcome these fundamental limitations, we propose the Physics-Informed Stochastic Configuration Machine (PI-SCM), a novel backpropagation-free framework for both forward and inverse problems in differential equations. The core mathematical contribution lies in the analytical evaluation of local Jacobians for nonlinear differential operators, which facilitates a linearized representation of the physical loss and projects it into a unified, linearized algebraic subspace. This reformulation allows for the explicit determination of optimal network weights via a sequence of generalized linear least squares solvers, effectively bypassing the iterative traps of traditional nonlinear optimizers. We develop a progressive algorithmic suite comprising localized construction (PI-SC-I), sliding-window updating (PI-SC-II), and global updating (PI-SC-III), and rigorously establish their universal approximation properties. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PI-SCM achieves high-fidelity predictive accuracy and robust parameter identification while accelerating the training process by orders of magnitude compared to standard PINNs. Our work provides a highly efficient and scalable foundation for next-generation, real-time Scientific Machine Learning applications.
tldr: This paper proposes a backpropagation-free neural network framework (PI-SCM) that efficiently solves nonlinear differential equations by linearizing the physical loss and using generalized linear least squares solvers.
motivation: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) suffer from computational bottlenecks and non-convex optimization challenges due to backpropagation and automatic differentiation.
method: PI-SCM analytically evaluates local Jacobians of nonlinear differential operators, projects the physical loss into a linearized algebraic subspace, and determines optimal weights via a sequence of generalized linear least squares solvers, with three progressive algorithmic variants (PI-SC-I, PI-SC-II, PI-SC-III).
result: Experiments demonstrate that PI-SCM achieves high-fidelity predictive accuracy and robust parameter identification while accelerating training by orders of magnitude compared to standard PINNs.
conclusion: PI-SCM provides a highly efficient and scalable foundation for real-time scientific machine learning applications.

title: Nil-Bohr Sets And Sums With Bounded Gaps
authors: Jianjie Zhao Yang Cao
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26568v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the relation between [MATH] sets and [MATH] sets. We prove that every [MATH] set is an [MATH] set, answering a question of Host and Kra. More generally, for a compact Hausdorff distal system whose Ellis group admits a closed filtration \[ E=E_1\supseteq E_2\supseteq\cdots\supseteq E_{d+1}=\{e\}, \ [E_j,E]\subseteq E_{j+1}, \] we prove that every return time set is an [MATH] set.
tldr: This paper proves a relationship between classes of integer sets arising from dynamical systems, answering a question of Host and Kra, but it is entirely unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: Host and Kra asked about the relation between certain combinatorial sets; this work aims to establish the inclusion and generalize to distal systems.
method: The authors analyze compact Hausdorff distal systems and their Ellis groups, using a filtration of the Ellis group to prove the set inclusion.
result: They prove that every set in one class is contained in another, and extend the result to return time sets in distal systems with a given Ellis group filtration.
conclusion: The paper provides a positive answer to Host and Kra's question and deepens the understanding of combinatorics via dynamics, but it is outside the scope of the research interests.

title: Galerkin Approximations To The Space Of Convex Bodies By Polytopes In Nondegenerate V-representation
authors: Janosch Rieger
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26615v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce finite-dimensional approximations to the space of convex bodies based on polytopes in vertex representation. For a prescribed set of directions, the admissible point configurations form a polyhedral convex subcone of the Euclidean vector space, described by a finite system of linear inequalities. The interior of this cone contains only nondegenerate representations, in which all parameter points are distinct vertices of the represented polytope. We study the geometry of the parameter cone, redundancies in its defining inequalities, and natural projections of convex bodies onto the resulting polytope spaces. We derive quantitative approximation estimates in terms of how densely the prescribed directions cover the unit sphere and construct nested Galerkin sequences whose approximation error converges locally uniformly to zero. Finally, we use these approximation properties to establish the convergence of finite-dimensional approximations of constrained global optimization problems in the space of convex bodies.
tldr: This paper introduces finite-dimensional Galerkin approximations to the space of convex bodies using polytopes in vertex representation, with applications to global optimization.
motivation: The motivation is to enable numerical approximation of convex bodies for solving optimization problems in that space, which is challenging with infinite-dimensional structures.
method: The method constructs polyhedral cones of admissible vertex configurations, studies their geometry, and derives approximation error bounds based on direction coverage on the unit sphere, leveraging nested Galerkin sequences.
