The exact decomposition solves all tested instances, including larger stress tests for which the extensive formulation becomes memory-limited, while the Lagrangian method provides substantially faster high-quality solutions.
tldr: Develops a bi-objective stochastic optimization model for healthcare facility resilience, balancing economic costs and social vulnerability in flood planning.
motivation: Flooding can damage healthcare facilities and cause costly evacuations; long-term investments need to consider both economic and social impacts under uncertainty.
method: Proposes a bi-objective two-stage stochastic optimization with hardening and evacuation decisions, solved via exact Benders decomposition and a scalable Lagrangian-dual method with primal recovery, embedded in an adaptive procedure for Pareto frontiers.
result: On a case study of 3,752 Texas healthcare facilities, minimizing economic costs alone can under-protect socially vulnerable areas; moderate trade-offs along the Pareto frontier substantially reduce disruption impacts at limited extra cost.
conclusion: The framework reveals important trade-offs between economic and social objectives and provides scalable exact and approximate solution methods for large instances.

title: Instantaneous Arithmetic Computation Via Ratio-encoding In Chemical Reaction Networks
authors: Badal Joshi David F. Anderson
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26305v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a general framework for instantaneous arithmetic computation using chemical reaction networks. Numerical values are encoded by ratios of species concentrations: an extended nonnegative value [MATH] is represented by a computational pair [MATH] through the ratio [MATH]. For this ratio encoding, our main theoretical result is a feedforward compositionality theorem: if a collection of modules satisfies two easily checked structural conditions, then any admissible finite feedforward composition computes the corresponding arithmetic expression instantaneously, meaning that every intermediate and output ratio is correct at every positive time. We make this framework concrete by constructing reaction network modules for four elementary operations---identification, inversion, multiplication, and addition---and verifying that each satisfies these structural conditions. As applications, we show that truncated power series and matrix products can be computed instantaneously using reaction networks whose size reflects the number of arithmetic operations in the underlying computation. We also extend the nonnegative ratio encoding to signed quantities by representing a real number as the difference of two nonnegative ratio-encoded values; this allows addition and multiplication over real-valued inputs. We discuss the practical implications of instantaneous computation, including its relationship to other resource constraints such as the number of chemical species required and the cost of reading out the final answer, which requires division and, in the signed case, rectified subtraction.
tldr: A framework for instantaneous arithmetic computation in chemical reaction networks using concentration ratio encoding, with a feedforward compositionality theorem.
motivation: To enable arithmetic operations to be performed instantaneously in chemical reaction networks, which could have applications in molecular computing.
method: Defines a ratio encoding for numbers and constructs modules for identification, inversion, multiplication, and addition; proves a feedforward compositionality theorem for these modules.
result: Compose these modules to compute any arithmetic expression instantaneously; demonstrate applications to power series and matrix products; extend to signed values.
conclusion: Provides a theoretical framework for fast arithmetic in chemical reaction networks, with implications for resource constraints.

title: Directional Optimality Conditions For Optimization Problems In Asplund Spaces
authors: Jane J. Ye Weihao Mao
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26328v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops directional necessary optimality conditions for constrained optimization problems in Asplund spaces. Under directional metric subregularity, we first derive a directional optimality condition in terms of limiting subdifferentials. We then introduce sufficient conditions for directional metric subregularity and establish their relationships with directional pseudo-normality and quasi-normality. For systems with joint constraints, we further propose a joint criterion for directional metric subregularity and use it to obtain necessary optimality conditions. The results not only extend several finite-dimensional directional constructions to an Asplund-space setting, but also yield conclusions that are new even in finite dimensions.
tldr: The paper develops directional necessary optimality conditions for constrained optimization problems in Asplund spaces under directional metric subregularity.
motivation: To extend finite-dimensional directional optimization constructions to infinite-dimensional Asplund spaces and obtain new results even in finite dimensions.
method: Utilizes limiting subdifferentials, introduces sufficient conditions for directional metric subregularity, and establishes a joint criterion for systems with joint constraints.
result: Provides directional necessary optimality conditions and criteria for subregularity, linking them to pseudo-normality and quasi-normality.
conclusion: Extends the theory of directional optimality to Asplund spaces, yielding results that are new even in finite-dimensional settings.

title: Isoperimetric Problems Related To Extremal Diameter Graphs In 3d: Theoretical And Numerical Aspects
authors: Beniamin Bogosel
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26395v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study optimization problems for separable functionals of the Euclidean or spherical lengths of dual edge pairs in finite extremal unit-diameter configurations in three dimensions. For a fixed diameter graph, these problems lead to nonconvex constrained optimization of the vertex coordinates. We first prove that a convergent sequence of extremal configurations retains an extremal geometric core after coincident points are merged and vertices incident to at most one diameter are removed. A spherical Crofton argument then gives a sharp lower bound for additive concave functionals, attained by the regular tetrahedron. We also analyze the effect of inserting or deleting dangling vertices. For the sum of products of spherical dual-edge lengths, we obtain an exact supremal reformulation of the three-dimensional Blaschke--Lebesgue area problem. The numerical study uses all 10,644 available extremal configurations with at most 16 vertices. We combine direct evaluation with gradient-based local optimization on each fixed graph and reconstruct the intrinsic diameter graph and its dual pairs after vertex collisions. For every supplied graph, the selected verified endpoint contains a regular tetrahedron. These computations do not certify the global maximum for any fixed graph, but they motivate structural conjectures connecting tetrahedral containment with the Blaschke--Lebesgue problem.
tldr: This paper investigates isoperimetric problems for extremal unit-diameter graphs in 3D, proving a sharp lower bound via spherical Crofton and linking to the Blaschke-Lebesgue problem, with numerical optimization on 10,644 configurations.
motivation: To understand geometric properties of extremal diameter graphs and their connection to classical isoperimetric problems like the Blaschke-Lebesgue problem.
method: Theoretical analysis using convergence properties of extremal configurations and a spherical Crofton argument, combined with gradient-based local optimization on finite graphs.
result: A sharp lower bound for additive concave functionals is attained by the regular tetrahedron, and an exact supremal reformulation of the 3D Blaschke-Lebesgue area problem is obtained; numerical results show tetrahedral containment for all supplied graphs.
conclusion: The computational findings motivate structural conjectures about tetrahedral containment and the Blaschke-Lebesgue problem, though no global maximum is certified.

title: Modular Topologies On Vector Spaces: Structure And Normability
authors: M. Khamsi, J. Lang, O. Mendez
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26428v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the topology generated by modular convergence on vector spaces endowed with a convex modular. Although modular convergence has long played a central role in the theory of modular function spaces, the topology it induces has, to the authors' best knowledge, not previously been studied as an independent mathematical object. Our principal result establishes that the modular topology is compatible with the vector space structure if and only if the underlying modular satisfies the [MATH]-condition. Consequently, the [MATH]-condition admits a purely topological characterization. We also show that the Luxemburg norm topology is the weakest first-countable topology containing all scaled modular topologies. We apply the theory to variable exponent sequence and Lebesgue spaces beyond the classical [MATH]-theory and present an application of our results to the minimization of the Dirichlet integral in [MATH] with unbounded exponent [MATH], which allows us to solve an open boundary value problem.
tldr: This paper studies the topology induced by modular convergence on vector spaces, characterizing when it is compatible with the vector space structure via the Δ2-condition.
motivation: The topology induced by modular convergence has not been studied as an independent mathematical object, and the authors aim to provide a topological characterization of the Δ2-condition.
method: The authors analyze the modular topology, establish its compatibility with the vector space structure iff the underlying modular satisfies the Δ2-condition, and relate it to the Luxemburg norm topology.
result: They prove that the Luxemburg norm topology is the weakest first-countable topology containing all scaled modular topologies, and apply the theory to variable exponent spaces and a Dirichlet integral minimization problem.
conclusion: The modular topology offers a natural framework for vector spaces with modulars, with implications for solving boundary value problems in variable exponent spaces.

title: Integrated Multi-Modal Transit Network Design Via Dynamic Line Generation
authors: Ning Duan, Oktay G\"unl\"uk, Samitha Samaranayake
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26444v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The integration of fixed-route public transit and on-demand mobility services presents both a modeling challenge and a computational opportunity for large-scale network design. We propose a flow-based mixed-integer programming formulation that jointly optimizes transit line planning and service frequencies while explicitly capturing first- and last-mile connectivity via on-demand services, under a fixed operating budget. To achieve tractability at urban scale, we develop a novel column generation heuristic scheme with tailored pricing subproblems. Applied to networks and demand in Boston and Chicago, the framework yields operationally feasible designs that substantially increase demand served. Relative to transit-only and on-demand-only baselines, ridership increases by up to 20.99% and 93.58% in Boston, and by up to 10.63% and 149.84% in Chicago. Compared to a multi-modal benchmark, our approach improves ridership by 5.42% and 5.80% in Boston and Chicago, respectively. These results demonstrate that (i) joint co-design of transit routes, frequencies, and on-demand legs within a unified optimization framework yields substantially greater ridership than single-mode or decoupled approaches under equivalent budget constraints; and (ii) the proposed formulation and column generation pricing scheme admit tractable, operationally feasible, high-performing solutions relative to tested baselines.
tldr: This paper proposes a column-generation-based optimization framework for jointly designing fixed-route transit lines and on-demand mobility services to maximize ridership under a fixed budget.
motivation: Integrating fixed-route and on-demand transit is challenging but can significantly improve urban mobility. The authors aim to address the computational complexity of large-scale network design.
method: They formulate a flow-based mixed-integer programming model and solve it with a novel column generation heuristic that includes tailored pricing subproblems.
result: Applied to Boston and Chicago networks, the framework increases ridership by up to 20.99% and 149.84% over transit-only and on-demand-only baselines, and by about 5-6% over a multi-modal benchmark.
conclusion: Joint co-design of routes, frequencies, and on-demand legs within a unified optimization framework yields operationally feasible, high-performing solutions, outperforming decoupled approaches.

title: Stability Analysis And Data-driven Verification Via Recurrent Lyapunov Functions
authors: Roy Siegelmann, Fernando Paganini, Enrique Mallada
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26447v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lyapunov's direct method is a cornerstone of stability and control, but it hinges on finding a Lyapunov function, a task demanding ingenuity or computation. A key difficulty is that every sub-level set of the function must be forward invariant, coupling its geometry to the system's trajectories. We relax this by replacing invariance with recurrence: a set is recurrent if every trajectory starting in it returns within a finite time. This yields the notion of a Recurrent Lyapunov Function (RLF), whose sub-level sets need only be recurrent. We show that, under mild conditions, RLFs guarantee stability, and we introduce stronger notions yielding asymptotic and exponential stability. We also give norm-based converse theorems: under the corresponding stability conditions, any norm is an RLF for their practical versions. We then develop GPU-based algorithms that certify (practical) stability from trajectory data alone, without a Lyapunov function. Certifying stability up to an [MATH]-neighborhood needs only [MATH] trajectory evaluations, with constants growing as the certified decay rate nears the true one, exposing an intrinsic performance-cost trade-off.
tldr: This paper introduces Recurrent Lyapunov Functions (RLFs) to relax the invariance condition in Lyapunov's direct method, enabling stability certification from trajectory data via GPU-based algorithms.
motivation: Finding Lyapunov functions is difficult and often requires ingenuity or computation, but the invariance condition on sub-level sets is overly restrictive.
method: Replace invariance with recurrence (trajectories return within finite time), define RLFs, prove stability guarantees, and develop GPU-based algorithms to certify stability from data without a Lyapunov function.
result: RLFs guarantee stability under mild conditions, with norm-based converse theorems and a trajectory complexity that scales with the desired accuracy, revealing a performance-cost trade-off.
conclusion: The proposed framework offers a data-driven approach to certify stability, potentially simplifying practical stability analysis.

title: Weight Distributions Of Single Parity-Check Product Codes Via Character Sums
authors: Sara D. Cardell Makson Miller Alves Ribeiro
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26457v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate structural and enumerative properties of binary single parity-check product codes. For each [MATH], [MATH] denotes the binary single parity-check code of length [MATH], consisting of all binary vectors of length [MATH] having even Hamming weight. We determine the generalized Hamming weight hierarchy of the product code [MATH], whose codewords can be represented as [MATH] binary matrices in which every row and every column has even Hamming weight. For the square product [MATH], we also determine the maximum codeword weight and prove that its homogeneous weight enumerator is symmetric if and only if [MATH] is even. After characterizing the dual code, we apply the MacWilliams identity in its Walsh--Hadamard formulation to derive an exact closed-form expression for the weight enumerator. By grouping the auxiliary binary vectors according to their Hamming weights, we obtain an explicit formula for each coefficient in terms of binomial coefficients and alternating convolutions. Finally, using Krawtchouk polynomials, we present an exact procedure for computing the full weight distribution without exhaustively enumerating all codewords. Numerical examples illustrate the formulas and verify the resulting computations.
tldr: This paper studies weight distributions of binary single parity-check product codes using character sums and MacWilliams identity.
motivation: Understanding weight enumerators of classical codes is important for error correction capabilities, though this work is purely classical.
method: The authors derive closed-form expressions for weight enumerator coefficients using character sums, MacWilliams identity in Walsh-Hadamard form, and Krawtchouk polynomials.
result: They obtain exact formulas for the weight distribution and an efficient computation procedure without exhaustive enumeration.
conclusion: The paper provides a complete enumerative and structural analysis of these codes, but has no connection to quantum information or related directions.

title: Local Product Structure Of Expansive Flows With Shadowing Property
authors: Xiao Wen
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26561v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that there exists a suspension flow defined over the full shift map which does not have local product structure. This gives a negative answer to an open problem posed by Gelfert-Kwietniak-Lima recently.
tldr: This paper provides a counterexample to an open problem by showing that a suspension flow over the full shift map lacks local product structure.
motivation: To answer an open problem posed by Gelfert-Kwietniak-Lima regarding the local product structure of expansive flows with the shadowing property.
method: Constructs a suspension flow over the full shift map and analyzes its dynamical properties to demonstrate the absence of local product structure.
result: Proves that there exists a suspension flow over the full shift which does not have local product structure, giving a negative answer to the open problem.
conclusion: The open problem is resolved negatively, indicating that expansive flows with shadowing do not always possess local product structure.

title: A Linear Mass-lumped Finite Element Method For The Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert Equation: Unconditional Energy Dissipation And Length Preservation
authors: Qiumei Huang, Binghong Li, Xiaoli Li, Cheng Wang, Jiang Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26687v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a linear, unconditionally energy-dissipative, mass-lumped finite element method for the highly nonlinear Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert (LLG) equation on quasi-uniform triangular meshes. The method is built on a projection strategy for enforcing the nonconvex pointwise constraint [MATH], whose simultaneous preservation with unconditional energy stability remains challenging for standard finite element discretizations. The key innovation is a unified hybrid finite element-finite difference framework that underlies both the design and the analysis of the proposed method. In the scheme construction, we exploit the weak formulation and nodal structure of mass-lumped finite element method, while incorporating suitable interpolation operators and a node-wise length-preserving mechanism inspired by finite difference discretizations. This combination yields a linear scheme that preserves the node-wise unit-length constraint and satisfies a discrete energy dissipation law. The same hybrid framework also plays a central role in the error analysis, where the weak formulation and quasi-uniform mesh structure of finite elements are combined with interpolation-based and nodewise finite difference method to control the strongly nonlinear damping term and to establish an optimal-order error estimate. More importantly, the proposed method provides a unified framework that systematically integrates the geometric flexibility of finite element method with the pointwise constraint-preserving property of finite difference method, and thus offers a general strategy for designing and analyzing structure-preserving discretizations of constrained dissipative systems. Numerical experiments, including a classical blow-up simulation, confirm the predicted accuracy, energy dissipation, and robustness of the method.
tldr: Develops a linear mass-lumped finite element method for the LLG equation with unconditional energy dissipation and length preservation.
motivation: To design a structure-preserving numerical scheme for the highly nonlinear LLG equation that maintains both pointwise length constraint and energy dissipation.
method: Combines finite element and finite difference ideas via a unified hybrid framework, using mass-lumping and interpolation operators to build a linear scheme.
result: Achieves unconditional energy dissipation and node-wise unit-length preservation, with optimal-order error estimates and numerical experiments.
conclusion: Provides a general strategy for structure-preserving discretization of constrained dissipative systems.

title: A Discontinuous Galerkin Discretization For The Sea Ice Dynamics
authors: Thomas Richter Emma Lagracie
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26810v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sea ice dynamics plays a crucial role in the Earth's climate system, making it an important component of weather and climate prediction models. Its numerical simulation remains challenging, however, as it exhibits complex mechanical behaviors due to a nonlinear ice rheology and interactions with external physical forcings. In particular, sea ice presents linear kinematic features (LKFs), i.e., narrow bands of intense deformation associated with processes such as lead opening or pressure-ridge formation. Accurately representing these features is necessary as they affect thermodynamics and ocean-atmosphere exchange. Yet their number, localization, and structure are highly sensitive to spatial resolution and to the chosen discretization of the sea ice velocity. In this work, we investigate the spatial discretization of Hibler's viscous plastic sea-ice model using a fully discontinuous Galerkin (DG) representation of all variables, including the velocity field. The ability of DG elements to represent discontinuities while having high order local polynomial approximation makes them well suited for resolving the complex ice deformation features, and insuring robustness towards mesh-induced numerical artefacts. We assess the fully DG method using an established sea ice dynamics benchmark and compare the obtained sea ice deformation with state-of-the-art discretizations. Additionally, we study the theoretical convergence of the modified Elastic-Viscous-Plastic (mEVP) formulation as a pseudo-time iterative solver for the viscous-plastic (VP) momentum equations. We prove the convergence of the underlying continuous pseudo-time dynamical system towards the viscous plastic formal limit, thereby providing a theoretical foundation for the use of mEVP as an iterative solver for Hibler's VP model.
tldr: This paper presents a discontinuous Galerkin discretization for sea ice dynamics to better capture linear kinematic features and provides a convergence analysis of the mEVP iterative solver.
motivation: Sea ice dynamics simulation is challenging due to nonlinear rheology and the need to accurately resolve linear kinematic features, which are sensitive to spatial discretization.
method: The authors use a fully discontinuous Galerkin (DG) representation for all variables, including velocity, to handle discontinuities and high-order approximation, and prove convergence of the continuous pseudo-time system for the modified Elastic-Viscous-Plastic (mEVP) solver.
result: The method is assessed on a standard benchmark, comparing with state-of-the-art discretizations, and theoretical convergence of mEVP to the viscous-plastic limit is established.
conclusion: The DG method shows promise for improving representation of complex ice deformation features and provides a theoretical foundation for mEVP as an iterative solver.

title: Spectral Convergence Of The Multipole Expansion Method For Acoustic Scattering In Three Dimensions
authors: Jun Lai Jinrui Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26884v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multiple scattering is a fundamental wave interaction phenomenon in acoustics and electromagnetics. The multipole expansion method (MEM) is the basis of many fast algorithms, such as the fast multipole method (FMM), for such problems. However, due to the infinitely many wave reflections involved, its convergence in three dimensions remains unexplored. In this paper, we prove spectral convergence of the MEM for time-harmonic acoustic scattering by finitely many well-separated spheres in three dimensions. Using a diagonally preconditioned single-layer formulation, we analyze the degree-[MATH] truncated system in a natural spherical harmonic energy space. We split the interaction truncation into target-side and source-side high-degree parts and choose a different representation for each: a projected Green-kernel representation for the former and degree-wise estimates of a translated spherical wave family for the latter. The resulting argument, based on Parseval's identity and the spherical harmonic addition theorem, provides a general framework for the convergence analysis of MEM and reveals the geometric and physical origins of the convergence factors. We also obtain a sharper estimate through the first-transfer analysis. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted spectral decay and the geometric convergence factor. This paves the way for the convergence analysis of a large class of fast algorithms for multiple scattering.
tldr: This paper proves spectral convergence of the multipole expansion method for acoustic scattering by well-separated spheres in three dimensions.
motivation: To rigorously establish the convergence of the multipole expansion method, which underpins fast algorithms like the fast multipole method, as its convergence in 3D was previously unexplored.
method: The authors use a diagonally preconditioned single-layer formulation, split the interaction truncation into target-side and source-side high-degree parts, and apply a projected Green-kernel representation for the former and degree-wise estimates for the latter, leveraging Parseval's identity and the spherical harmonic addition theorem.
result: They prove spectral convergence with a geometric convergence factor, and numerical experiments confirm the predicted decay.
conclusion: This work provides a general framework for convergence analysis of multipole expansion methods and paves the way for analyzing fast algorithms for multiple scattering.

title: Waveguiding In Systems Of High Contrast Resonators: Theory And Fast Computations
authors: Habib Ammari, Bowen Li, Borui Miao, Jiayu Qiu, Lara Vrabac
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26906v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we study guided modes in systems of high-contrast resonators near nonzero interior Neumann frequencies, beyond the subwavelength regime. In the regular exterior regime, where the exterior Dirichlet problem is well-posed at the reference wavenumber, we introduce an infinite-dimensional frequency-dependent capacitance operator obtained by compressing the exterior Helmholtz Dirichlet-to-Neumann map to the traces of the interior resonant Neumann eigenspaces. We prove the norm-resolvent convergence of the continuous problem to this discrete effective operator as the contrast [MATH], and derive first-order asymptotic formulas for compact-defect frequencies and line-defect band functions. We then establish exponential off-diagonal decay of the capacitance coefficients by a Combes--Thomas argument, yielding an exponentially accurate truncation of the discrete operator, and show that its retained coefficients can be computed from local Helmholtz problems. At the physical frequency, this local approximation converges exponentially under a uniform stability assumption for the growing finite-cluster problems. The stability assumption can be removed by introducing a vanishing complex absorption together with a Hermitian symmetrization. In particular, an absorption parameter of order [MATH], together with interaction truncation and patch radii of order [MATH], suffices to preserve the [MATH] accuracy of the first-order high-contrast expansion of the defect eigenfrequencies, yielding a fast computational method. Numerical experiments for dipole and quadrupole resonances illustrate the accuracy, exponential locality, and applicability of the discrete model to straight and bent waveguides generated by material or geometric detuning.
tldr: This paper studies guided modes in high-contrast resonator systems beyond the subwavelength regime, introducing a capacitance operator and asymptotics for fast computation.
motivation: To understand waveguiding in high-contrast resonator systems and develop efficient numerical methods for computing guided modes and defects.
method: The authors compress the exterior Helmholtz Dirichlet-to-Neumann map to interior resonant eigenspaces, prove norm-resolvent convergence, derive first-order asymptotic formulas, and employ a Combes-Thomas argument for exponential decay of coefficients, enabling local approximations with absorption.
result: They obtain exponentially accurate truncations and fast computational methods, validated for dipole and quadrupole resonances in straight and bent waveguides.
conclusion: The proposed discrete model is both accurate and exponentially local, providing an efficient tool for simulating waveguides with high-contrast resonators.

title: Stiff Norm Estimates For Variable-Stepsize Peer Two-Step Methods
authors: Bernhard A. Schmitt Jens Lang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26913v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Peer two-step methods are attractive for the numerical solution of stiff initial value problems because they combine favorable features of Runge-Kutta and multi-step methods, including high-order accuracy, strong stability properties, and the avoidance of order reduction. This paper develops rigorous norm estimates for the propagation operators of variable-stepsize diagonally-implicit [MATH]-stable Peer methods applied to stiff semi-linear systems. The analysis relies on a class of Peer methods whose propagation matrices possess a grid-independent left eigenvector, enabling the construction of suitable matrix norms for entire coefficient families. We show that this class contains [MATH]-stable methods of stage order [MATH] and super-convergence of order [MATH] with [MATH] stages, exceeding the classical stage-order barrier [MATH] of irreducible [MATH]-stage diagonally-implicit Runge-Kutta methods, and construct such methods up to order 5. Achieving high stage order is one of the principal advantages of Peer methods, especially for stiff differential equations where it helps mitigate order reduction. The resulting theory provides uniform stability bounds for stiff semi-linear problems on variable grids and establishes a foundation for further applications to optimal control and related boundary value problems. Comparative numerical results are presented for three classical stiff benchmark problems, including three novel Peer two-step methods of order 3, 4, 5, and four singly diagonally implicit Runge-Kutta methods with a first explicit step of stage order 2 and order 3, 4, 5, and 6.
tldr: This paper develops rigorous norm estimates for variable-stepsize Peer two-step methods for stiff semi-linear systems, demonstrating high stage order and uniform stability.
motivation: Peer two-step methods are attractive for stiff ODEs because they combine Runge-Kutta and multi-step advantages, but lack rigorous stability bounds on variable stepsizes.
method: The authors analyze a class of Peer methods with grid-independent left eigenvectors to construct suitable matrix norms, and design new methods up to order 5.
result: They provide uniform stability bounds for stiff semi-linear problems and construct novel Peer methods of order 3, 4, and 5, comparing them with SDIRK methods.
conclusion: The proposed Peer methods achieve high stage order without order reduction, offering a promising alternative for stiff systems and extending to optimal control.

title: Linear Response For Random Systems With A Cusp
authors: Davrbek Oltiboev, Karim Rakhimov, Marks Ruziboev
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26969v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study i.i.d.\ random compositions of cusp tent-like interval maps having a common cusp point and a common cusp value. For cusp exponents [MATH], we prove that the associated annealed transfer operators have a spectral gap on [MATH] and [MATH]. For all sufficiently small perturbations of the probability law, there is a stationary density [MATH], unique among stationary densities belonging to [MATH]. Moreover, the map [MATH] is differentiable at [MATH] in [MATH], and we obtain an explicit linear response formula.
